description: "I AM FREE, I WILL WHATEVER it takes- go the mile"
summary: Long space missions expose astronauts to five hazards: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and a hostile closed environment. These cause immune changes, bone and muscle loss, cardiovascular problems and behavioural health problems. Help is delayed, so astronauts must spot changes in themselves. The Space Apps challenge asks for a visual tool that gathers indicators and helps them judge and act on their own health.
details:
The idea in one line

An astronaut-first, offline-first self-check tool that compares each person to their own baseline, explains every result, and says what to do and when to call the ground. Guidance, never diagnosis.

What is measured

Hazard Indicators

  • Radiation: Dose against a mission budget, body temperature.
  • Isolation: Mood, sleep, workload.
  • Distance: Escalation guidance, offline mode, shareable report.
  • Gravity: Heart rate, blood pressure, exercise load, strength.
  • Closed Environment: Blood sugar, nutrition and hydration, temperature.

The brief names six indicators (blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep, mood). The plan added exercise load and radiation dose to carry the gravity and radiation hazards.

What I built

  1. ART style prompt to get the project outline: the plan i thought off revised through and rewritten using Act as / Request / Terms and then Prompted into Claude to build out the initial versions.
  2. v1 demo: clickable figure, Time Warp and scenarios (it felt like documentation).
  3. v2 app (current): green and white, human-centred flow: Home, a one-minute guided check-in, indicator detail with trend and actions, and a report for the flight surgeon.

Scenarios, data and plan

  • Scenarios: Skipped Gym, Isolation Slide, Radiation Event, Sugar Swing, Recovery Arc (stretch: EVA heat stress, cabin CO2).
  • Data: a browser simulator, shaped by public NASA bedrest and PhysioNet patterns, clearly labelled simulated.
  • Run plan: prep (10 to 13 Nov), then a 48-hour hackathon (14 to 15 Nov) with scope cut-lines and a feature freeze at hour 30. Never cut: the figure, the traffic lights, the Learn and Act panels, Time Warp, one working scenario.
  • Design: Streamlit for the front ends, FastAPI for the back ends, and SQLite through SQLModel. Both APIs read the same SQLite database.
  • Open questions: official deliverables, which indicators to go deepest on, clinician review, which datasets to cite, camera input.

I CANNOT call this A FINISHED project but its CREATIVE

There is still so much development to be done which isnt possible in a 48 Hours hackathon, a lot of refinement and error correction has to be done. Fitness tracker is fine and all. Why not something specific- something deeper catering to the need of the Astronauts in space, heck even those going to MARS its a worth while creative project in my opinion in terms of Space research.

Other Considerations

Originally i thought to make it like a game, then i realised you don't really need a game to keep such highly motivated astronauts engaged- So i made a health tracker. I thought also to add a mini doll like figure which monitors their activity but then it felt more underwhelming- It can be worked upon and refined later into the development cycle.
